comparison: Both address imaging and gene expression evidence for olfactory receptor downregulation (C5-C8, C10-C12). OpenEval finds the evidence SUPPORTED with appropriate controls and reversibility. Peer reviewers rate it UNCERTAIN, explicitly stating 'further studies are required to determine whether and how olfactory sensory neurons and odorant receptors mediate the effects of diacetyl,' indicating the mechanistic link remains unclear despite convincing phenotypic effects.

Both evaluate in vitro HDAC inhibition data (C16-C20). OpenEval and peer reviewers agree this is SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers describe the work as 'interesting and important' and note diacetyl 'can act as a histone deacetylase (HDAC) inhibitor' without challenging the biochemical data. OpenEval highlights IC50 quantification and benchmarking against known inhibitors.

Both assess histone acetylation evidence (C21-C25). Both rate as SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers state diacetyl can 'trigger wide changes in gene expression' and treat the histone acetylation data as convincing demonstration of HDAC inhibitory activity. OpenEval emphasizes specificity for H3K9 and effects at physiologically relevant concentrations.

Both evaluate Drosophila RNA-seq data (C26-C29). Both rate as SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers explicitly state 'the effects on gene expression changes and degenerative phenotypes are convincingly shown.' OpenEval supports the findings but notes concerns about batch effects and biological replicate sufficiency (n=2) that peer reviewers do not mention.

Both assess mouse lung transcriptome data (C30-C33). Both rate as SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers note gene expression changes in 'both Drosophila and mice' are 'convincingly shown.' OpenEval supports the findings but raises cautions about high exposure concentrations (peak 1920 ppm) and uncertainty about human translation of ACE2 downregulation that peer reviewers do not explicitly address.

Both evaluate comparison with established HDAC inhibitors and reversibility (C34-C37). Both rate as SUPPORTED with perfect claim overlap. Peer reviewers consider this part of 'convincingly shown' gene expression changes supporting the HDAC inhibition mechanism. OpenEval notes the strong statistical significance and appropriately acknowledged differences in gene sets between treatments.

Both address brain transcriptome and blood-brain barrier penetration (C38-C41, C71-C72). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting gene expression changes don't definitively prove BBB crossing and could result from indirect systemic effects. Peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED, acknowledging diacetyl 'trigger[s] wide changes in gene expression' with effects 'convincingly shown,' without questioning the BBB penetration inference.

Both evaluate brain gene expression changes (C42-C46). Both rate as SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers describe these as part of 'convincingly shown' brain gene expression changes supporting therapeutic potential. OpenEval supports the findings but notes the connection between mouse brain gene expression and neuroblastoma cell proliferation is correlative rather than mechanistic.

OpenEval R8 includes neuroblastoma cell proliferation data (C47-C48, C73) along with brain gene expression. Peer R9 specifically addresses these cell proliferation claims. Both rate as SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers note 'HDAC inhibitors not only reduce cancer cell proliferation' as part of study findings. OpenEval notes specificity for neuroblastoma but based on limited cell lines (n=3).

Both evaluate Huntington's disease model data (C49-C55, C74). Both rate as SUPPORTED with perfect claim overlap. Peer reviewers explicitly state diacetyl provides 'suppression [of] neurotoxicity in a Drosophila model of Huntington's disease' with 'degenerative phenotypes convincingly shown.' OpenEval emphasizes the ~50% reduction in degeneration with strong statistical significance and consistency with prior HDAC inhibitor work.

OpenEval R10 addresses ecological/physiological context (C1, C4, C78). Peer R11 is a comprehensive background claims evaluation including these. Both rate as SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers do not challenge background information supporting the study's 'interesting and important' rationale. OpenEval notes these establish biological relevance and experimental design rationale.

OpenEval R11 addresses natural occurrence and sources of diacetyl (C2-C3, C56-C57). Peer R11 includes these among comprehensive background claims. Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes quantitative context from banana concentration data. Peer reviewers accept all background information without challenge.

OpenEval R12 addresses safety context and toxicity literature (C59-C63). Peer R11 includes these in comprehensive background evaluation. Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes balanced presentation of risks including GRAS status and cigarette smoke exposure data. Peer reviewers do not challenge this safety context.

OpenEval R13 addresses HDAC biology and therapeutic background (C64-C66, C79-C81). Peer R11 includes these in comprehensive background evaluation. Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes this context is necessary for interpreting significance of volatile HDAC inhibitors. Peer reviewers accept this as supporting the study's rationale.

OpenEval R14 addresses microbiome-host interaction context (C58, C76-C77). Peer R11 includes these in comprehensive background evaluation. Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval frames this within broader microbiome research field. Peer reviewers do not challenge this contextual information.

OpenEval R15 includes summary claim C68 (diacetyl as HDAC inhibitor) which overlaps with peer R2's evaluation of HDAC inhibition mechanism. Both rate the HDAC inhibitor conclusion as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes these are summary statements supported by detailed experimental results. Peer reviewers describe this as 'interesting and important' work.

OpenEval R15 includes summary claim C69 (gene expression changes) which overlaps with peer R3's evaluation of histone acetylation effects. Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval treats this as synthesis of major findings. Peer reviewers note diacetyl can 'trigger wide changes in gene expression.'

OpenEval R15 includes summary claims C67 and C70 (transcriptional changes) which overlap with peer R4's evaluation of Drosophila RNA-seq data. Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes these appropriately synthesize major findings. Peer reviewers state effects are 'convincingly shown.'

OpenEval R15 includes summary claim C70 (transcriptional changes) which overlaps with peer R5's evaluation of mouse transcriptome data. Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval treats this as synthesis statement. Peer reviewers note gene expression changes are 'convincingly shown.'

OpenEval R15 includes summary claim C75 which peer R11 includes in comprehensive background evaluation. Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes this synthesizes major findings. Peer reviewers accept this as part of the study's overall rationale and context.
